facts.text: Cassopolis was laid out in 1831 and became the county seat the same year, cementing its early role in regional governance.
The village’s name honors Lewis Cass, a New Hampshire native who served as a U.S. senator and later governor of Michigan.
During the 1870s Cassopolis boasted a bustling commercial scene with dry goods, hardware, and even a machine shop and foundry.
Cassopolis was a key stop on the Underground Railroad, offering shelter to escaping slaves seeking freedom in the North and Canada.
The Cass District Library’s Local History Branch, located in Cassopolis, serves as a treasure trove for researchers exploring the area’s past.
In 1899 the new courthouse was completed, and a decade later Andrew Carnegie funded the construction of the La Grange Township Library in 1908.
